sections.overview: The mandarinfish is a small, brightly coloured dragonet native to the western Pacific.
sections.identification: Its blue body bears orange, red and yellow markings; males have a much longer first dorsal spine.
sections.habitat: It inhabits shallow coral reefs and lagoons, commonly over coral rubble and silty bottoms, from about 1 to 18 m deep.
sections.diet: It feeds on small bottom-dwelling invertebrates, including tiny crustaceans and worms among reef growth.
sections.behavior: It moves close to the reef, often in pairs or small groups, and is also collected for the marine aquarium trade.
sections.reproduction: At night, pairs rise above the reef and release eggs and sperm into the water.
sections.ecology: Its diet consists of small reef-associated prey, while spawning briefly takes place in open water above the reef.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a global IUCN assessment of Least Concern, dated 2018.
